CVE-2026-54658 SQL injection: trailing backslash quote-escape payload in web/proxy request parameters AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the specific exploitation primitive from CVE-2026-54658 — a parameter value using a trailing backslash to escape the closing single quote (\') followed by injected SQL — inside HTTP request query strings captured by WAF/proxy or web-tier logs. This is the on-the-wire signature of the escapeValue() bypass, not a generic SQLi template. Rationale: Targets the advisory's exact mechanism — 'a trailing backslash to escape the closing quote' — as the \'(-encoded %5c%27) sequence immediately preceding SQL keywords, which is far more specific than generic OR-1=1 SQLi. Payloads in POST/JSON/gRPC bodies won't appear in URL query strings (noted limitation); pair with UC-3 for backend confirmation. Defender endpoint telemetry has no HTTP request-parameter source, so defender_kql is intentionally blank. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54658 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcc-39rp-hh9p
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate URLs containing Windows file paths that end in a backslash before a quoted token
  • Security scanners (Burp/ZAP/Nuclei) running authorized SQLi test suites against the app
  • Regex-heavy application parameters that naturally contain 'or'/'select' substrings adjacent to escaped characters
  • Marketing/analytics query strings with URL-encoded punctuation that coincidentally matches
  • WAF already blocking and re-logging the same payload multiple times per request
Suppression filter
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(union(%20|\+|\s)+select|;(%20|\+|\s)*(drop|insert|update|delete)|--|/\*)"
Response runbook
1) Triage: decode the RequestURL, confirm the \'-then-SQL structure targets a hypequery-backed endpoint, and check the source IP's request history for enumeration/fuzzing bursts. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, add a rule rejecting backslash-immediately-before-quote in parameters, and confirm the target service is on @hypequery/clickhouse 2.0.2+. 3) Hunt: correlate the request timestamp against UC-3 ClickHouse query-log/syntax-error events on the backend, and review DB audit logs for successful UNION/stacked queries or data reads following the request.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RequestURL)
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(%5c|\\)(%27|')(?:%20|\+|\s)*(or|union|select|and|;|--|%3b)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

goshs launched with WebDAV + --no-delete (CVE-2026-64863 vulnerable config) AIWeaponization High
Surfaces goshs (<=2.1.3 / <=1.1.4) instances started with the WebDAV listener AND the --no-delete guard, the exact configuration CVE-2026-64863 silently defeats via the MOVE verb. Detecting the running exposure lets the SOC find at-risk artifact servers before an attacker abuses MOVE to delete/clobber files. Rationale: Anchors on the goshs binary plus the exact two-flag combination (--no-delete AND --webdav/-w) named in the PoC; this pairing is the vulnerable state itself and virtually never occurs benignly. Cross-checked GitLab Advisory DB and TheHackerWire (fixed in 2.1.4, vulnerable <=2.1.3). WebDAV MOVE request succeeding against a goshs server (CVE-2026-64863 exploitation) AIExploitation Medium
Flags HTTP MOVE requests that return 201/204 on a goshs-fronted WebDAV endpoint. MOVE is a rare verb in enterprise traffic, and against goshs <=2.1.3 a successful MOVE deletes the source file regardless of --no-delete, so a 2xx MOVE is direct evidence of the bypass being exercised. Rationale: Uses the article's exploit primitive verbatim: MOVE returning 201 (new dest) or 204 (existing dest overwritten). MOVE is near-absent in normal enterprise HTTP, so a successful one against a WebDAV host is high-signal for the bypass. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/goshs.de/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/goshs-webdav-move-allows-file-deletion-and-overwrite-cve-2026-64863/

  • SharePoint/IIS WebDAV file reorganisation
  • Backup or sync tooling that renames files via MOVE
  • Authorized pentester interacting with their own goshs instance
Suppression filter
| where DstHostname !in~ ("sharepoint.corp.local", "webdav-sanctioned.corp.local")   // exclude approved WebDAV shares
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the destination server and confirm it is goshs (Server response header 'goshs/vX.Y.Z') running --webdav --no-delete; if so a 2xx MOVE is exploitation, not routine WebDAV. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the proxy/WAF and firewall the WebDAV port to trusted ranges, then upgrade goshs to 2.1.4+. 3) Hunt: correlate the same source IP for prior DELETE 403s and subsequent MOVEs (bypass-probe pattern) and audit the served directory for deleted/overwritten files.
ImWebSession

| where HttpStatusCode in ("201", "204")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

goshs --no-delete bypass probe: DELETE 403 then MOVE 2xx on same path AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates a blocked DELETE (403) followed within seconds by a successful MOVE (201/204) on the SAME URL from the SAME client — the exact signature of an attacker discovering that --no-delete blocks DELETE but not MOVE. This is the CVE-2026-64863 bypass being deliberately probed and exploited. Rationale: Encodes the article's core finding literally: 'DELETE is correctly blocked (403) but MOVE still destroys existing files.' Same-path DELETE-403 -> MOVE-2xx from one client within 60s is a near-unambiguous bypass probe, hence alerting-tier. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/goshs.de/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/goshs-webdav-move-allows-file-deletion-and-overwrite-cve-2026-64863/
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WebDAV client that gets a 403 on DELETE (permissions) then legitimately renames the file via MOVE by coincidence on the same path
  • Automated sync tool retrying a delete as a move-to-trash operation
  • QA/validation script exercising both verbs against a test WebDAV endpoint
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request sequence for the source IP/URL and confirm the target is goshs --no-delete; the 403-then-2xx ordering on an identical path is the bypass being demonstrated. 2) Contain: block the source IP, firewall the WebDAV port, and upgrade goshs to 2.1.4+. 3) Hunt: expand to all MOVE/COPY activity from that source across other goshs hosts and inventory files that vanished or changed content in the served directories.
let Window = 60s;
let Deletes = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where HttpMethod == "DELETE" and HttpStatusCode == "403"
    | project DelTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, Url;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod == "MOVE" and HttpStatusCode in ("201", "204")
| join kind=inner Deletes on SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, Url
| where TimeGenerated between (DelTime .. DelTime + Window)
| project DelTime, MoveTime = TimeGenerated, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, DelTime), SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode
| order by MoveTime desc

WebDAV MOVE returning 204 No Content (destructive Overwrite:T against existing file) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects HTTP MOVE requests that return 204 No Content against a WebDAV endpoint. Per the goshs PoC, a MOVE to a NEW destination returns 201 Created, while a MOVE with Overwrite:T over an EXISTING file returns 204 and triggers RemoveAll(dst) — so a 204 MOVE is the destruction-of-existing-data variant of CVE-2026-64863. Rationale: Grounded in the PoC status codes: bypass 1 (new dest) -> 201, bypass 2 (Overwrite:T over victim.txt) -> 204. The 204 specifically maps to RemoveAll on an existing file, making it the destructive case worth alerting on even without request-header logging. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/goshs.de/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/goshs-webdav-move-allows-file-deletion-and-overwrite-cve-2026-64863/
ATT&CKT1485 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WebDAV client overwriting an existing document via move/rename (e.g. save-over workflows)
  • File-sync tooling that replaces files using MOVE with overwrite semantics
  • Backup rotation renaming over an existing target on a sanctioned WebDAV share
  • Authorized pentest reproduction of the overwrite PoC
Suppression filter
| where DstHostname !in~ ("sharepoint.corp.local", "webdav-sanctioned.corp.local")   // exclude approved WebDAV shares
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the destination is goshs --no-delete and identify which file the 204 MOVE overwrote (Url path); the pre-existing file's contents were destroyed via RemoveAll. 2) Contain: block the source, firewall the WebDAV port, upgrade to goshs 2.1.4+, and restore the overwritten file from backup. 3) Hunt: search the same source for additional MOVE 204s and any preceding directory listings (PROPFIND) used to pick targets.

| where HttpStatusCode == "204"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

goshs process deleting/renaming files while running --no-delete (impact confirmation) AIActions on Objectives High
Confirms actual data loss from CVE-2026-64863 on the host: goshs itself performs the file rename/RemoveAll when serving a MOVE. This hunts FileDeleted/FileRenamed events whose initiating process is goshs — impossible under a correctly enforced --no-delete guard, so any hit is proof the MOVE bypass executed. Rationale: Ties the wire-level bypass to on-disk impact: the article states MOVE calls fs.Rename (removes source) and RemoveAll(dst); both surface as goshs-initiated FileDeleted/FileRenamed. Filtering InitiatingProcessCommandLine for --no-delete makes any hit a contradiction of the intended guard, hence near-zero FP. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/goshs.de/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/goshs-webdav-move-allows-file-deletion-and-overwrite-cve-2026-64863/

  • Authorized red-team operator intentionally testing MOVE against their own goshs --no-delete instance
  • goshs temp-file cleanup on shutdown writing/removing its own scratch files
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the deleted/renamed file paths under the goshs served root and correlate with the corresponding WebDAV MOVE request time; confirm the file was one that should have been protected. 2) Contain: stop the goshs process, preserve the host for evidence, and restore lost files from backup; upgrade to 2.1.4+. 3) Hunt: pivot on the goshs process_guid to enumerate every file it deleted/renamed and cross-reference proxy logs for the originating client IP(s).

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-64863", "CVE-2026-50138")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-64863", "CVE-2026-50138")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-64863", "CVE-2026-50138")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-64863", "CVE-2026-50138")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
